moves.name: Open on the finished result already running, no intro
moves.how: First frame is the output working: the dashboard, the edited video, the AI on a real call. Explain after.

moves.name: Lead with a specific number plus the outcome, mirrored on screen
moves.how: '37 AI agents run my entire company.' The count goes in the first sentence and in a label on frame one.

moves.name: 'X just dropped' or 'Claude can now' news framing
moves.how: Frame it as fresh news about a known tool, with the logo or repo on screen.

moves.name: Name the wrong way or the overpriced thing, then promise the fix
moves.how: Call out the common method, a flaw in a popular tool, or an expensive offer in the first line. The fix follows in the same breath.

moves.name: Stack two versions in one frame so the comparison is the hook
moves.how: AI over real, result over source, rich over poor. Label both panels. No explanation needed in the first second.

moves.name: Say the video you are watching was made by the tool
moves.how: The reel is its own proof. State it in the first seconds and show the styling already applied.

moves.name: Open on a borrowed clip, famous name or pop-culture reference
moves.how: Start on someone the viewer already knows (a creator, a celebrity program, a movie scene), then pivot to your point.

moves.name: Start mid-action or mid-conversation
moves.how: No greeting, no setup. The first words are the command to the AI, the first list item, or a line from an exchange already underway.

moves.name: One text label over a single absurd or tense frame
moves.how: 'POV:', 'Average X user:', 'Wait for it'. The viewer reads the joke before the audio starts.

moves.name: Name a specific profession and its constraint in the first line
moves.how: 'A lawyer's Instagram with no time to record.' 'Over 15 years a doctor.' Speaks to one audience by name.

moves.name: Say the count up front and label every step or item on screen
moves.how: 'Three easy steps.' Each one gets a spoken number and a persistent on-screen tag so the viewer always knows where they are.

moves.name: Tour your real system, one area at a time
moves.how: Name the whole (six departments, seven branches), then click into each so the screen changes every few seconds.

moves.name: Put an obstacle, a skeptic moment or a failure inside the demo
moves.how: The slot is unavailable. Someone asks 'are you an AI?'. The task fails without the tool, then works with it. A demo with friction has a story.

moves.name: Hold a bonus, trick or 'crazy part' for late in the reel
moves.how: 'Here's the trick.' 'But here's the crazy part.' 'We're not done yet.' A marked second peak right before the ask.

moves.name: Escalate in beats and end on the strongest line with no sign-off
moves.how: Each beat is bigger than the last. The final line is the punchline or the most emotional item, and the video ends there.

moves.name: Keep it under 15 seconds in one shot so it loops
moves.how: One idea, one shot, short enough to replay before the viewer decides to leave.

moves.name: Chain prompts on screen, each one visibly upgrading the last result
moves.how: Type a plain prompt, show the result in seconds, then the next prompt builds on it.

moves.name: Anchor against a price, then show it free
moves.how: Show what others charge ($700, $8,000, a subscription), strike it, and give the free route.

moves.name: Run it as a recurring verdict format (Fact or Hype, Yay or Nay)
moves.how: A named test with a visible verdict box that stays on screen until the result.

moves.name: Tell an automation as a story with a ridiculous payoff
moves.how: Trigger, consequence, consequence, absurd final action. One scene per step.

moves.name: Graphic or screen on top, face below, captions on the seam
moves.how: Top 40 to 65 percent is a stage for screens, cards or diagrams. The face stays visible underneath. Captions sit where the two meet.

moves.name: Put a visual on every spoken noun, changing every 1 to 3 seconds
moves.how: Each tool, number or object named gets its own image, card or screenshot at the moment it is said.

moves.name: Film the real screen with a phone instead of screen recording
moves.how: Handheld, pointing with a finger or pen, pushing in physically on the result. It reads as live and real.

moves.name: Word-by-word captions, one to three words at a time
moves.how: Big, bold, usually caps, one accent colour for the key word.

moves.name: One uncut take, with on-screen labels doing the motion
moves.how: No hard cuts. A counter, labels or a diagram change while the shot holds.

moves.name: Keep a live state indicator on screen: counter, checklist, progress bar, verdict box
moves.how: Something on screen updates as the video goes, so the viewer can see progress and waits for it to finish.

moves.name: Use clean designed mocks or diagrams in place of real footage
moves.how: Purpose-built UI cards, pixel diagrams or animated mock screens stand in for screen recordings.

moves.name: Keep a face in frame during the screen demo
moves.how: A small bubble, a reaction layer or a second person stays visible while the screen plays.

moves.name: Annotate by hand: circle, strike through, highlight
moves.how: Red circle on the number, strike through the wrong way, yellow highlighter on the key phrase of a screenshot.

moves.name: Demonstrate the technique on the video itself
moves.how: Explain text-behind-head while text sits behind your head. Draw the script structure as you speak it.

moves.name: One comment keyword as the last spoken line, mirrored on screen
moves.how: The ask is the final thing said, with the keyword as text. Nothing after it.

moves.name: No ask in the video; end on the payoff
moves.how: The reel ends on the punchline, the verdict or the last line. Any keyword lives in the caption only.

moves.name: Make the offer early or keep it on screen throughout, not only at the end
moves.how: Offer the keyword the moment the asset is first mentioned, or pin it as a static bar, then repeat it last.

moves.name: Show the actual deliverable right before the ask
moves.how: The repo page, the guide cover, the DM arriving. The viewer sees what they get before being asked.

moves.name: Cut back to your face for the ask
moves.how: Leave the screen or b-roll and deliver the keyword to camera.

moves.name: Ask for a follow plus the comment
moves.how: 'Follow me and comment KEYWORD.' Two actions in one ask.

moves.name: Show your own real numbers on screen
moves.how: Your analytics, your payments, your comment count, your member count. Circled or highlighted.

moves.name: Prove it is real, not a concept
moves.how: Click into it, open the actual file, show the call log, hold up the phone with the text it sent, name the exact repo.

moves.name: Admit the catch, the limit or your own critique
moves.how: 'The only catch.' 'It zooms too much.' 'You may need to ask for a revision.' Honest friction before the ask.

moves.name: Back the claim with real headline or source screenshots
moves.how: Current headlines, a README, a news pop-in, shown at the moment the claim is made.

moves.name: Name the 'this ends in a course' objection and cross it out
moves.how: Show the paid course, strike it, promise free help.

moves.name: Topic: AI agents running a company, a personal OS, or a Jarvis
moves.how: Dashboards of agents by department, a voice assistant doing a real errand, a content OS.

moves.name: Topic: Claude edits your video
moves.how: Claude Code with skills, Remotion, ChatCut, DaVinci handoff, auto music.

moves.name: Topic: Claude plus your own health and fitness data
moves.how: Whoop export or self-hosted replacement, Strava and Oura through a database, a Telegram health coach, pose tracking.

moves.name: Topic: Claude for content research, hooks and scripting
moves.how: Claude as strategist, connecting Instagram, watching videos, script structure, hook teardowns, saved reels to skills.

moves.name: Topic: AI video generation tricks
moves.how: Higgsfield Genjutsu, Kling Motion Control, Seedance video-to-video, AI hooks and text effects, face-swap parody.

moves.name: Topic: AI in medicine and clinics
moves.how: ER command center, a surgeon's 10 year prediction, ambient scribes, patient conversion system, eldercare camera, longevity companies.

moves.name: Topic: a new connector, MCP, repo or plugin for Claude
moves.how: 'Install these 4 MCPs', the Indeed connector, Agent Reach, 11 free plugins, data-broker removal, Project NOMAD.

moves.name: Topic: AI as the butt of the joke
moves.how: The chatbot apologizes for the disaster it caused, hidden 'thinking' lines, usage-limit memes.
